evidence.note: Luo et al., FSE 2014, 161 flaky-test fix commits: Async Wait 45% (34% use a fixed time delay; 54% fixed with waitFor), Concurrency 20%, Test Order Dependency 12% (74% fixed by cleaning shared state).
Make tests isolated (each test independent, own storage/data); use web-first assertions and auto-waiting locators instead of manual waits.

ts-test-fixed-sleep.whyNotLinter: The Promise+setTimeout idiom and custom `sleep`/`delay` helpers have many shapes; telling a wait-for-work sleep from simulated latency inside a mock needs meaning. Existing plugins only ban the Playwright/Cypress APIs by name.
ts-test-fixed-sleep.aiRelevance: When a test fails intermittently, agents add or lengthen a sleep until it passes locally — the classic flaky-test fix Luo et al. describe.

evidence.note: ImpossibleBench (ICLR 2026): agents pass impossible tests by modifying/deleting tests, special-casing test inputs, operator overloading, state recording; Claude models mostly modify tests; cheating rates up to 92% (GPT-5, one variant).

Vendor guidance on agent behavior: models sometimes hard-code values or special-case test inputs; ask for general solutions that 'work for all valid inputs, not just test cases'. Read via search summary, not fetched in full.
Konstantinou et al.: LLM-generated oracles tend to encode actual (possibly buggy) behaviour rather than expected behaviour (cited via Banik et al. ref [9]).

ts-test-title-contradicts-assertions.whyNotLinter: Comparing natural-language test titles with assertion semantics is exactly the kind of judgment no linter can make.
ts-test-title-contradicts-assertions.aiRelevance: ImpossibleBench: when tests conflict with the spec, agents (Claude models especially) edit the test to pass; the visible residue is a title that no longer matches the assertion.

ts-test-shared-mutable-state.whyNotLinter: jest/vitest `require-hook` (opt-in) only flags setup code outside hooks; whether a later test reads what an earlier test wrote needs data-flow judgment across test bodies in the snippet.
ts-test-shared-mutable-state.aiRelevance: Agents write a sequence of tests as a script ('creates the user', then 'updates the user') that passes only in file order and breaks under sharding, `--shuffle`, or `.only`.

ts-test-special-case-in-source.whyNotLinter: `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'test'` is matchable, but most such checks legitimately swap infrastructure; only reading what the branch returns tells special-casing from configuration.
ts-test-special-case-in-source.aiRelevance: ImpossibleBench documents special-casing test inputs and conditions as a common way agents make failing tests pass; Anthropic's prompting guide warns about it explicitly.
